title: Finite bounded-degree Q3 Friedrichs form closure and volume-uniform shifted order
question: For a fixed finite Q3 graph with bounded degree, do the exact onsite and bond forms have a common Friedrichs form domain and a volume-uniform shifted form order?
method: Use the exact onsite square completion to obtain the per-site lower bound -5/12 and choose the coercive per-site shift 17/12.
Reuse the exact quartic bond envelope B_ij <= (10/3)(h_i+h_j)+304/45 and recompute the shifted remainder 304/45-2(10/3)(17/12)=-121/45.
Apply the standard semibounded real Schrodinger-form closure theorem at each fixed finite graph; bond positivity gives one form-domain inclusion and the shifted envelope gives the reverse inclusion.
Sum the local bound over graphs of degree at most six to obtain K_on <= K_edge <= 21 K_on, then run independent Fraction-only grids and Lean R302 for the exact polynomial and rational constants.
finding: Primary 32827/32827, independent 26251/26251, integrated 12/12, and Lean R302 PASS. The fixed finite graph form theorem applies because chi,g>0, c,lambda>=0, the polynomial potentials are real and locally integrable, and the negative part is bounded. The closures share the quartic form domain, the associated Friedrichs operators exist for each finite graph, and the degree-six shifted order is K_on <= K_edge <= 21 K_on with per-site shift 17/12.
decision_reason: The prior EXP-001130 conditional form comparison is now unconditional at the declared fixed-finite-graph form level: the standard semibounded Schrodinger form theorem supplies closure/Friedrichs realization, while the exact bond envelope supplies common-domain equality and a bounded-degree uniform order. The remaining obstruction is specifically the weighted product-domain identity and its cutoff/beta/modular transfer, not finite form closure.
